correctness.rationale: Fan's coprime-index criterion gives the admissible exponent classes. Equality of two admissible two-term functions forces equality of their reduced supports and coefficients; the only cross-index possibility reverses the support, forcing d'=-d and a=a'=1. The identity q^h ell_{e-h}=ell_e-ell_h proves admissibility of the reversed exponent, while the coefficient condition restricts the collision to odd q and odd e. Exact-integer checks support the counting formulas across both parity regimes.

originality.rationale: Fan arXiv:2609.20354v1 explicitly counts distinct functions for d=1 and classifies every fixed coprime index d, but no all-coprime-index equality-collision theorem or global count was located in the inspected version. Hou--Pallozzi Lavorante study a broader equivalence relation rather than equality as functions. Exact and synonymous searches found no matching prior theorem; unindexed contemporaneous work remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The result closes the natural enumeration problem after the coprime-index classification and identifies the unique cross-index collision mechanism. It shows precisely when naive multiplication of the fixed-index count is valid and supplies the exact parity correction when it is not.
